extractedText: Explore Modern Shenzhen – China’s Innovation Hub Author Thomas Schulz | Passionate traveler and writerLast updated: June 8, 2026 sun jib, pixabay Shenzhen is one of the most remarkable cities on Earth. In just four decades, this former fishing village in southern China’s Pearl River Delta transformed into a 17-million-resident megacity that rivals Silicon Valley for tech innovation and Hong Kong for skyline drama. Whether you’re drawn to cutting-edge gadget markets, world-class theme parks, subtropical beaches, or Cantonese dim sum, this Shenzhen travel guide covers everything you need to plan your trip. Its border with Hong Kong makes it one of the most accessible mainland Chinese cities for international travelers. Upcoming Events in ShenzhenDateTitleDetails2026-05-01 to 2026-07-26Glamorous Xianbei TreasuresAn exhibition at the Shenzhen Museum’s Ancient Art Division showcasing 157 sets of treasures from the Murong Xianbei culture of roughly 1,600 years ago, including an ornate tree-shaped gold headdress, armour and murals. It traces migration, cultural fusion and daily life across the ‘Three Yan’ kingdoms. Free admission, running through late July. A fascinating window into ancient history. [Source]2026-06-09 to 2026-06-11Intertextile Shenzhen Apparel Fabrics 2026A major apparel-fabrics and textile trade fair at the Shenzhen Convention & Exhibition Center, covering fabrics, fibres, designs and innovative manufacturing technology. The previous edition drew nearly 650 exhibitors from 13 countries and around 40,000 visitors. Free pre-registration for trade buyers. A key event for the textile industry. [Source]2026-06-19 to 2026-06-21Shenzhen Dragon Boat Festival (Duanwu)Over the three-day Dragon Boat Festival holiday, Shenzhen hosts dragon boat races on local waterways alongside the traditional eating of zongzi. The races are free, family-friendly public events celebrating one of China’s most cherished festivals. A lively way to mark the start of summer. [Source]2026-06-12Fan Ni x Chen Sa: Classical Enigmas — SZSOA Shenzhen Symphony Orchestra subscription concert at the Shenzhen Concert Hall, pairing conductor Fan Ni with celebrated pianist Chen Sa as part of the 2025/2026 season. It is one of several June classical programmes at the hall. Ticketed. A refined evening of orchestral music in Futian. [Source]2026-05-28Ray Chen Violin RecitalA solo recital by internationally touring violinist Ray Chen at the Shenzhen Concert Hall at 19:30. It sits within a strong late-May run at the hall that also includes a Yuja Wang piano recital. Ticketed. A chance to hear a charismatic soloist in the city’s premier concert venue. [Source]2026-05-31 to 2026-06-01Shenzhen Children’s Day Family ConcertA family-oriented concert tied to China’s Children’s Day, staged across the 31 May and 1 June weekend at 15:00 at the Shenzhen Concert Hall. Designed for families with children, it offers accessible afternoon programming. Ticketed. A delightful outing for young audiences and their parents.
